assertion: The rate of women dying from pregnancy or childbirth has dropped to pre-pandemic levels, as mental health issues become the leading cause of deaths and Black mothers continue to die at higher rates than others
searched: Texas MMMRC 2026 biennial report maternal mortality ratio
independent_value: Report: 2024 MMR 20.5, 'a similar rate as before 2020' (2013-2019 range 17.0-20.7)

assertion: In 2024, the maternal mortality ratio ... was 20.5, a decrease from 23.5 in 2021 (which excludes COVID-related deaths), and slightly above what rates were in 2019
independent_value: 20.5 and 23.5 (COVID excluded) confirmed; 2021 MMR including COVID was 39.1; 2019 was 17.2

assertion: More than three-quarters of deaths were found to be preventable in both 2021 and 2024, although it represented a slight decrease from 80% from the committee's previous report
Pregnancy-related mortality rates among Black women was the highest among all racial and ethnic groups and 2.4 times higher than non-Hispanic white women.
Severe maternal morbidity rates ... increased from 80.4 to 83.5
inaccuracy: The article says 83.5 and implies a 2021 baseline; the report says 83.9 in 2024, up from 80.4 in 2023, per 100,000 delivery hospitalizations.

assertion: Black women in 2024 experienced severe maternal morbidity at a rate of 146.2 per 100,000 births, more than double that of white women in the same time frame.
inaccuracy: The article says per 100,000 births; the report's denominator is delivery hospitalizations. The ratio, 146.2 vs 65.7 (2.2x), supports 'more than double'.

assertion: infection was the leading cause of death in 2021 and mental health in 2024.
independent_value: Infection 55% (n=33, 91% COVID) in 2021; mental health 20% (n=12 of 59) in 2024

assertion: a quadrupling in the number of cases where violence like suicide or homicide was a factor, from 5% to 19%. While obesity as a contributor halved from 63% to 29%, every other major factor nearly doubled
inaccuracy: The article calls 5% to 19% a quadrupling (it is 3.8x, of a share not a count) and says every other factor 'nearly doubled'; nicotine rose 3% to 19% and mental disorders 8% to 19%.

assertion: More than half of the pregnancy-related deaths in both 2021 and 2024 were women who were on Medicaid, but decreased slightly from 57% to 53%. In both years, 22% of deaths were women who paid out of pocket
independent_value: Medicaid 57%->53%; out of pocket/no payor 22% both

assertion: Most of the report's 11 recommendations on improving maternal health outcomes in Texas were the same as the 2024 report
independent_value: Report lists 11 recommendations; the count matches. The overlap with the 2024 report is the reporter's characterization and was not compared line by line.

assertion: State officials were supposed to release Sept. 1 but delayed until after the midterm elections
independent_value: Due Sept. 1, delayed (2025 state law permits to December); released Nov. 13. DSHS denies election motive; the piece reports that denial.

assertion: State Rep. Charlene Ward Johnson, D-Houston, filed a bill ... That bill passed the House but not the Senate.
independent_value: HB286 filed 11/09/2026; HB3339 passed House 5/16/2025, received by Senate 5/19/2025, no further action

assertion: I am glad the Department has finally decided to release the MMMRC's 2026 report, but it remains unacceptable that they delayed its release by more than 2 months
speaker: Rep. Donna Howard
independent_value: Sept. 1 to Nov. 13 is about 2.4 months; 'unacceptable' is opinion
